title: SLA-driven response commitments for DPAs, vendor questionnaires, and regulatory requests
creator: Jordan Lee
description: Objective: Define and launch an SLA-driven intake and response flow for Data Processing Agreements (DPAs), vendor security questionnaires, and regulatory data requests (GDPR/HIPAA) to reduce enterprise sales friction and improve legal/engineering throughput. This ticket covers design of tiers, routing logic, response timelines, playbooks, and a lightweight dashboard for tracking SLA compliance.
acceptance_criteria: Signed-off SLA tiers (e.g., Self-serve, Standard Enterprise, Priority) with max response windows defined for legal, security, and engineering review
Intake form and metadata fields implemented in first-line triage (source, customer tier, requested deliverable, deadline, regulatory scope)
Routing map that auto-assigns to 'Legal', 'Security Review', or 'Eng Support' based on taxonomy plus escalation rules for 'Priority' tier
Library of pre-approved answer templates and redlines for DPAs and common questionnaire sections, stored in Confluence/Drive with versioning
Runbook for SLA breaches (notifications, auto-escalation, and fallback copy for sales), plus two-week pilot with two enterprise customers
Dashboard card in Console->Enterprise Intake showing SLA adherence, average response time, and open items by tier
notes: Background: Sales and Solutions Engineering report repeated delays on DPA and questionnaire turnaround causing multi-week contract stalls.
Trade-offs: Faster TAT for higher-tier customers increases legal/security workload; propose limited operational hours + callback SLAs for lower tiers.
We will prioritize templated responses for repeated questionnaire items to reduce engineer time (configurable templates by model/product).
Related artifacts: Draft runbook in Confluence (link below) and sample GitHub PR with intake form schema for the helpdesk.
decision_log: 2025-02-16: Agreed to three SLA tiers (Self-serve: 7 business days, Standard: 5 business days, Priority: 2 business days) — decision owners: Product (Jordan), Legal (Marta Ruiz), Security (Ethan Park)
2025-02-18: Chose to implement intake metadata that includes 'data-sensitivity' and 'regulatory-scope' fields to drive auto-routing. Engineering feasibility OK for minimal schema changes.
2025-02-19: Legal requested final sign-off on DPA templates before pilot; blocking until legal review complete.
comments: 2025-02-15 Jordan Lee: Filed initial ticket after weekly sales sync; priority set P1 due to three stalled contracts.
2025-02-16 Marta Ruiz (Legal): Affirmed willingness to own templates but needs two business days per template review. Requested clear versioning.
2025-02-17 Ethan Park (Security): Asked for 'regulatory-scope' field to capture HIPAA/GDPR/SOC2 flags; noted need for access control on template bank.
2025-02-19 Priya Sethi: Drafted runbook and uploaded sample DPA templates to Drive; opened PR for intake schema. Marked legal review as blocker.
2025-02-20 Sales feedback: Pilot customers A and B confirmed readiness to trial Priority tier SLA in exchange for formal DPA language.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Legal team becomes bottleneck for template approvals. Mitigation: stagger templates, create a review SLA, and allow pre-approved 'clauses' to be reused.
Risk: Engineering time required for redlines. Mitigation: invest in templating engine and map common questionnaire items to canned answers maintained by Product.
Risk: SLA commitments create expectation of product changes. Mitigation: clearly document scope and 'out of scope' items and require explicit change requests for feature work.
outcome_metrics: Reduce average enterprise questionnaire turnaround from 21 business days to <=7 business days for Standard tier within 8 weeks of rollout
Achieve >=90% on-time SLA compliance for Priority tier during a 4-week pilot
Reduce legal review hours per questionnaire by 40% through templating and pre-approved clauses
